meta.title: Context Engine Aggregate Graph — Discovery and POC Decision
meta.description: A source-backed architecture decision explaining why the current aggregate is not queryable, where CBM cross-repo matching fails, and what the hybrid POC must prove.

props.title: Build the semantic audit layer, not another graph concatenator.
props.subtitle: Native cross-repo edges remain structural evidence; Context Engine owns the business-semantic read model.

props.content: The existing aggregate is a scale projection with no materialized nodes, the live query path fans out across repos instead of traversing a merged graph, and current CBM indexes contain no cross-project edges. The shortest credible POC is a query-time semantic joiner that treats inferred links as candidates until evidence and audit gates admit them.

props.title: Recommended: hybrid semantic read model
props.content: Rebuild each leaf structural graph when its declared baseline branch changes. Let native CBM transport matching contribute raw evidence where extraction is complete. Let an agent-driven POC resolve scope and assemble candidate chains from raw graph results plus `.ulta/entities`. Context Engine must normalize, audit, rank, and expose every chain with evidence state and explicit gaps.
props.next: Run a zero-write three-repo semantic POC and an isolated native cross-edge benchmark before drafting the implementation proposal.

props.label: 01 · Current state
props.title: The aggregate exists as a plan, not as a traversal surface
props.subtitle: Four observed facts separate the live implementation from the intended company graph.

props.title: Observed implementation ledger
props.summary: Current checkout and live MCP queries only.

items.claim: The June aggregate candidate is not materialized and contains zero graph nodes and links.
items.detail: Five source repos are repeated to simulate sixty; both candidate graphs report materialized false.

items.claim: The aggregation implementation namespaces and copies repo-local nodes and links without synthesizing cross-repo edges.
items.detail: Every copied node and link receives a virtual repo id; no cross-repository join phase exists.

items.claim: The Context Engine query command returns one result block per repository rather than traversing an aggregate graph.
items.detail: The function loops over selected repositories and invokes the provider independently.

items.claim: Context Engine's codegraph provider and Codebase Memory MCP are separate graph systems today.
items.detail: The package depends on `@colbymchenry/codegraph`; no CBM provider adapter exists under context-engine/src.

items.claim: A merge-triggered leaf rebuild and central delta refresh are running in production.
items.detail: The repo docs describe this target flow, but no CI configuration or current execution receipt was found in the checked-out source repos.

props.title: The aggregate receipt proves scale, not usefulness
props.claim: A large projected graph count is not evidence of a queryable company graph.
props.evidence: The codegraph candidate projects 2,005,032 nodes and 4,766,316 links by repeating five inputs across sixty virtual repos, while the persisted graph is only 3,543 bytes and is marked `projection_plan_only`.
props.limitation: This receipt is dated 12 June 2026 and does not prove current source-index freshness.

props.title: Ownership boundary
props.content:
## Four responsibilities, one query contract

Source repository CI owns one leaf rebuild for the branch declared in `repo-manifest.yaml`. It publishes a generation and evidence receipt; it does not build a company graph.

Codebase Memory and other providers own structural extraction. Their cross-project edges are raw evidence, never canonical business truth.

Context Engine owns normalization, semantic identity, evidence admission, freshness, conflicts, candidate boundaries, promotion, and the shared `graph.query` / `graph.explain` response contract.

The agent or skill owns query decomposition during the POC: `ScopeResolver → EvidenceRetriever → SemanticJoiner → ChainAuditor`. Those routines consume manifest and ontology data; they do not memorize the org chart in prompt prose.

props.label: 04 · Options
props.title: Three routes, one that survives production scrutiny
props.subtitle: The comparison separates POC speed from long-term authority.

props.title: Why the hybrid wins
props.content: It preserves the cheapest useful behavior from both alternatives. Native provider edges stay available when the source extractor can prove them. Agent reasoning accelerates discovery, but every inferred hop remains candidate evidence. Context Engine supplies the missing durable contract: typed identity, audit, freshness, conflicts, confidence, and a business-facing query response.

props.label: 05 · Proof plan
props.title: Prove the joins before building the service
props.subtitle: The POC is intentionally bounded to three repos and one business path.

props.title: Semantic baseline
props.content: Run the agent/skill against `web-site`, `exp-graphql`, and `orch-buy` without graph mutation. Resolve scope from the manifest, retrieve raw graph hits, join typed `.ulta/entities`, and return admitted paths, candidates, and gaps.

props.title: Native matcher
props.content: Run CBM cross-repo intelligence in isolated graph stores. Capture the number and shape of `CROSS_*` edges, plus every miss caused by unresolved constants, dynamic paths, or missing handler identity.

props.title: Decision receipt
props.content: Compare business-question accuracy, evidence-ref coverage, wrong admitted edge rate, regeneration time, and manual edge count. Promote to proposal only if the hybrid materially improves answer quality without hiding candidate joins.

props.title: Discovery score
props.claim: The hybrid is ready for a bounded POC, not implementation promotion.
props.evidence: Direct source inspection, live CBM schema/search/trace queries, existing entity projections, and prior design lineage produce a weighted proof score of 0.83.
props.limitation: No merge-triggered rebuild, isolated native cross-edge pass, or end-to-end business query service was exercised.

rows.decision: Context usefulness and query proof precede graph promotion.
One Context Engine CLI dispatches provider build, query, benchmark, and status.
rows.use: Reuse provider boundaries, not old projections.

rows.decision: Interview-driven query plans and negative controls support estimates.
rows.use: Use as POC question gold set.

rows.decision: Context Engine owns evidence boundaries, graph semantics, and CLI/API/MCP parity.
Typed semantic projections sit over raw provider graphs; inference cannot admit truth alone.
Business users do not choose repos; benchmark hybrid delta refresh against commerce questions.
Repo CI rebuilds leaf evidence; Context Engine aggregates and serves it.
Semantic planner is the decision reference; workstream remains paused before execution.
